chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a group, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from his brother al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about a man who is in an open land, having only one garment upon him, and he becomes in a state of janabah in it, and he has no water with him—what should he do? He said: "He performs tayammum and prays naked while seated, and gestures."

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: entered the state of janabah requiring ritual purification
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: performs tayammum as a substitute for ghusl or wudu (ablution) when water is unavailable
key_terms.يُومِئُ: indicates the prayer motions by gesture

ai.seo_question: What should a person in janabah do if he has no water and only one garment in the wilderness?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person in a state of janabah who has no water and only one garment that cannot be used while remaining clothed. The Imam عليه السلام instructs him to perform tayammum and offer salat seated and without full bodily movements, indicating prayer by gesture in a state of necessity.
